Operator:  
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Consumer Brands Inc., or GCB, Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. Please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.  

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Vice President of Investor Relations.  

Alex Rivera:  
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss GCB's Q3 2024 results. With me on the call are Jamie Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Maria Lopez, Chief Financial Officer; Sarah Chen, Chief Marketing Officer; and David Kim, Chief Supply Chain Officer; along with other members of our leadership team.  

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.  

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Jamie Thompson.  

Jamie Thompson:  
Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. GCB delivered a solid Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment marked by persistent inflation, shifting consumer behaviors, and geopolitical headwinds, while remaining focused on executing our strategic priorities under our Next Generation Growth strategy.  

Our discussion today will cover our overall financial performance across segments and regions; brand performance and innovation efforts; supply chain and operational efficiency; marketing and promotional activities; sustainability initiatives; and our outlook for the remainder of the year.  

I will now turn the call over to Maria Lopez to provide more detail on our financial results.  

Maria Lopez:  
Thank you, Jamie. Good morning, everyone. As Jamie mentioned, we delivered a standout quarter amid a dynamic CPG landscape. Consolidated net sales reached $15.4 billion, up 5.2% year-over-year, with organic sales growth—our gold standard metric excluding acquisitions, divestitures, and FX—coming in at 4.8%. This marks our third consecutive quarter of organic acceleration, outpacing the total CPG category growth of 2.8% per NielsenIQ data. Adjusted EPS was $1.42, up 9% from last year, reflecting 180 basis points of operating margin expansion to 22.4%. Gross margins stood at 48.2%, up 170 basis points year-over-year and 120 basis points sequentially, thanks to targeted pricing actions averaging 6% across the portfolio, favorable commodity mix shifts, and productivity savings from our $250 million annual supply chain optimization program. Operating income was $3.3 billion.  

Let me walk you through the key performance highlights by segment. Our powerhouse Personal Care division—featuring brands like VitalGlow skincare and AquaFresh oral care—surged 7.3% organically to $6.2 billion, fueled by double-digit market share gains in premium segments. Household penetration for VitalGlow reached 28% in North America per IRI scans, up from 24% a year ago, driven by our Clean Beauty platform tapping into the $15 billion U.S. clean beauty trend with microbiome-targeted formulations. Food & Beverages grew 3.8% organically to $5.1 billion, with snacks leading at 6% thanks to velocity on NutriCrunch protein bars—now the number two brand in the $4 billion bar category behind Clif—amid consumer trade-down from pricier indulgences. Household Essentials was up 1.2% to $4.3 billion, offset by 12% growth in eco-pod innovations capturing share from Tide Pods in the sustainability aisle.  

Regionally, North America remains our growth engine at 6.5% organic sales growth to $9.8 billion, or 63% of total sales, with e-commerce at 22% of sales—up from 18%—via Amazon exclusives and DTC TikTok Shop integrations. Premiumization drove 65% of NA volume from super-premium SKUs priced 20% above averages. EMEA grew 2.1% organically to $3.2 billion through 4% pricing and SKU rationalization, pruning 15% of low-velocity items for winners like EuroFresh plant-based yogurts. APAC accelerated to 5.9% at $2.0 billion, led by China rebound up 12% post-zero-COVID in beauty and India snacking. Latin America was resilient at 1.8% to $0.6 billion, with Brazil beverages gaining 2 points share per Kantar.  

Operationally, our AI-powered demand sensing across 80% of factories cut forecast error by 25% and inventory days to 65, locking 70% of 2024 commodities at 5% below spot. Cash flow from operations hit $2.3 billion, up 15%, funding $1.1 billion in repurchases and a 7% dividend hike to $0.78 per share. Net debt to EBITDA is 2.1x with $4.5 billion liquidity.  

Diving deeper into geographic performance, developed markets like North America, Western Europe, and Australia/New Zealand—62% of revenue—delivered steady 2.5% organic growth to $9.4 billion, with flat volumes offset by 3% price/mix. North America grew 3% on Beauty & Wellbeing, with Radiance Renew serums gaining 8% share; snacks and beverages dipped 1% on inflation. Western Europe was 1.8% at $3.2 billion, mitigating EU plastic regs with PureFlow recyclable bottles now 25% of SKUs, margins up 50 bps to 22.5% via Project Nexus procurement. Australia/NZ flat but GreenBite bars at 12% ACV. Volumes pressured by private label gains, but pricing and premium health shifts provided stability.  

Emerging markets—38% of revenue—posted 12% organic growth to $5.8 billion, 15% above pre-COVID, with volumes up 9% and price/mix +3% despite FX like Argentine peso devaluation. APAC ex-Japan/Australia led at 15% on $2.5 billion, India SparkleClean sachets up 20% via JioMart, China PearlWhite Pro rebounding. Latin America 14% on $1.8 billion, Brazil refreshers up 18%. Middle East/Africa 11%, Nigeria ZestCrunch snacks 25% volumes. Emerging margins hit 23.8%, up 120 bps via AI route-to-market and precision fermentation. Developed offers margin stability and 75% of FCF; emerging drives 45% incremental sales, total share +1.1 points globally.  

On gross margins specifically, the 48.2% rate—our strongest in five years—reflected net revenue of $15.4 billion minus $7.4 billion COGS. Pricing delivered 5.2% realization, outpacing inflation by 300 bps; elasticity -2.1 via AI pricing on 10TB data. Mix added 80 bps with Elevate organic extensions up 15%, AUR +3.8% in NA e-com at 22%. Savings contributed 90 bps: $180 million quarterly from ZBB 2.0, palm oil contracts 12% below spot via RSPO, 30% rPET with Berry Global, new Monterrey facility at 92% utilization cutting conversion 8%. NA at 50.1% with 6% pricing; Europe 44.8% countering energy via outsourcing; APAC/LATAM 47.5% on FX and China teas share gains. Freight eased 10%, nearshoring at 40%. PackLight cuts virgin plastic 50% by 2027, blockchain cocoa with Barry Callebaut.  

For guidance, we're raising full-year FY2024 gross margin to 42.5%-43.5%, implying 200 bps expansion vs. FY2023's 40.7%; Q4 at 43%-44% on NA seasonal strength offset by holiday freight. Tailwinds: pricing 120 bps (5-7% increases, elasticity minimal like PepsiCo Frito-Lay); productivity 110 bps ($85 million Q3 from Margin Accelerator, AI hedging palm/cocoa, APAC plant closures, FourKites routing); mix 70 bps (premium/sustainable at 28% sales, 55% margins). Headwinds: 2-3% input inflation (sugar +4%), 1.5% USD FX, Q4 freight/labor 15 bps. Assumptions: commodities flat-+2% (palm $950/MT, cocoa $6,000/MT), +1% volumes skewed premium, regional 44% NA etc., no disruptions. Targeting 45%+ by FY2026 via premiumization to 35%, zero-based COGS.  

These results tie into our four key strategic priorities: Accelerated Portfolio Premiumization, with 5.2% organic overall but 12.4% premium led by VitalCore plant-based up 28% at 65% ACV, PureThirst +3.2 share points, 14 new items at 85% repeat; drove 210 bps expansion insulating 4-6% inflation. Supply Chain Resilience, $300 million invested in AI demand sensing like P&G, dual-sourcing 90% top ingredients, new Midwest facilities; turns 8.2x saving $280 million WC, Precision Procurement $180 million YTD, EMEA localized 40% cutting leads 22 days to 98% OTD. Digital Commerce Acceleration, e-com 22% NA sales via AR try-ons lifting conversions 35%, DTC $450 million run-rate at 40% margins, APAC SnackHub +45%, Shopify AOV +22% to $48, 2.5 points growth. Sustainable Innovation Leadership, Planet Positive Pledge net-zero 2035, 100% rPET by 2028 reducing 25,000 tons, EcoBarrier wipes 12% LATAM share, 15% brand equity uplift, 62% growth from sustainable SKUs.  

Holistic: Q3 EPS $1.42 up 11% ex-FX, FY guidance $5.65-$5.75, share +90 bps (NA +1.4, APAC +2.1), ROIC 18.2%. Ahead: $500 million productivity, 20+ innovations, 6-8% organic.  

Next, I'll turn the call over to Sarah to discuss marketing and brand performance.  

Sarah Chen:  
Thank you, Maria. We saw strong performance in our core brands this quarter. Our marketing team executed with precision, achieving portfolio ROAS of 4.8x, up 15% YoY from 4.2x, outperforming the 3.5x-4x industry benchmark per Nielsen and ahead of Kellogg's or General Mills amid TV fragmentation.  

Digital now 62% of $320 million A&M spend, programmatic/CTV 7.1x ROAS via Trade Desk/Roku lookalikes on 45 million loyalty data; RMNs like Amazon DSP/Walmart Connect drove $420 million sales at 5.9x. Social commerce TikTok/Instagram $92 million DTC lift, 4.2% conversions via micro-influencers. Performance marketing 55% budget, A&M/sales 12.5%, CAC down 22% to $18, LTV +16% to $142.  

Flagship Refresh Everyday for VitalQuench ($2.8 billion franchise vs. Gatorade/Powerade) lifted HHP 22%, $185 million incremental, share +1.8 to 14.2%, repeats +28%. Snack Smarter for EverCrisp ($1.2 billion vs. Frito-Lay) 6.2x ROAS on $45 million, velocity +17%, trial +35%, AOV +12%. CleanGlow sampling 3.4x quick payback.  

NA 5.2x ROAS, VitalQuench +2.4 points at Costco; Europe 4.9x on CleanGlow eco-claims vs. Persil; APAC 5.7x China/India Diwali +31%; LATAM 4.3x Brazil Carnival. Tech: $25 million data clean room Google DV360/Snowflake for 32% targeting, AI Adobe Sensei testing 1,200 assets +28% CTR, AR zero-party +40% engagement.  

Precision shopper missions on 12 million households, contributing 28% to 7.2% organic growth. Q4 ROAS to 5.2x on $1.4 billion, VitalFuture sustainability for premium pricing.  

Following me, David will update on supply chain initiatives.  

David Kim:  
Thank you, Sarah. We continue optimizing our supply chain for efficiency and cost reduction, implementing new technologies to enhance responsiveness. Post-pandemic, we've invested $300 million in zero-base redesign—AI demand sensing, multi-sourcing 90% top 20 ingredients, three new U.S. Midwest aseptic facilities derisking ports. Inventory turns 8.2x from 6.9x, WC down 15% or $280 million. Precision Procurement with blockchain soy saved $180 million YTD, 12% ahead, offsetting 70% raw inflation. EMEA localized 40% production amid 25% energy spikes, leads -22 days, OTD 98%. AI across 80% factories cut forecast error 25%, inventory 65 days. Nearshoring 40% supply within 2,000 miles, dynamic routing slashed freight 12% vs. Red Sea issues. Emerging Scale AI route-to-market cut DSD 8%, fermentation raw variance 12%. Sustainability: regenerative ag 40% cocoa/coffee, Scope 3 -18% ahead EU regs. This funded 50 bps SG&A deleverage while growing top-line, supporting margin rebuild.  

On sustainability, Planet Positive Pledge targets net-zero Scope 1&2 by 2035, 100% recyclable packaging 2028, 70% beverages rPET cutting 25,000 tons virgin plastic, EcoBarrier biodegradable wipes 95% water-efficient at 12% LATAM flushable share. 15% brand equity uplift per Nielsen, 300 bps higher margins, LATAM regenerative coffee 20% savings, ESG financing 75 bps below LIBOR. 62% growth from sustainable SKUs growing 2x faster per Unilever data.  

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.  

Operator:  
Thank you. Instructions as before. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.  

John Smith:  
Could you provide more insight into the geographic performance, particularly in developed versus emerging markets?  

Jamie Thompson:  
Thanks, John. As Maria detailed, we saw a clear divergence that underscores our balanced portfolio. Developed markets at 62% of revenue grew organically 2.5% to $9.4 billion, resilient through pricing and premium shifts despite volume softness from inflation and private labels gaining 1.5 points. North America led at 3% on beauty share gains, Europe 1.8% countering regs with innovations like PureFlow, Australia strong in plant-based. Emerging markets shone at 12% organic to $5.8 billion, volumes +9%, led by APAC 15% on India/Indonesia, LATAM 14% Brazil/Mexico, MEA 11% Nigeria/South Africa snacks and beauty. FX shaved reported growth, but local sourcing boosted emerging margins to 23.8%. This mix—developed for cash flow stability, emerging for velocity—drove +1.1 points total share, with us leaning in via $800 million emerging capex for D2C and regen ag. We expect developed 2-4%, emerging 11-13% FY24 at constant FX.  

Operator:  
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with JPMorgan.  

Lisa Chen:  
How are you managing inventory levels given the current economic uncertainty?  

Maria Lopez:  
Great question, Lisa. Inventory discipline is core to our resilience. Turns improved to 8.2x from 6.9x YoY, reducing working capital 15% or $280 million, now at optimal 65 days via AI demand sensing rolled out 80% factories, cutting forecast error 25%. We've dual-sourced 90% top ingredients, built Midwest facilities derisking disruptions, and nearshored 40% supply. In uncertainty, Precision Procurement blockchain saved $180 million YTD offsetting inflation, while dynamic routing and FourKites cut freight 12%. This keeps us agile for volatility like cocoa surges or port issues, funding repurchases without straining liquidity at $4.5 billion.  

Operator:  
Our next question comes from Mike Patel with Morgan Stanley.  

Mike Patel:  
Can you discuss the progress on your sustainability goals and any related cost implications?  

David Kim:  
Thanks, Mike. Sustainability drives $2 billion revenue opportunity and margins. Planet Positive Pledge on track: net-zero Scope 1&2 by 2035, 100% recyclable packaging 2028, 70% beverages now 100% rPET saving 25,000 tons plastic YTD like Coke's PlantBottle. EcoBarrier wipes captured 12% LATAM share, regenerative coffee/LATAM ag co-ops 20% costs savings, ESG financing cheaper. Scope 3 down 18% via 40% regen cocoa/coffee ahead EU regs. Consumer pull: 62% growth from green SKUs, 15% equity uplift, 300 bps higher margins, 62% millennials prioritize per surveys +8 loyalty. Costs offset by eco-premium +3%, PackLight bio-plastics below $1,200/ton, RSPO palm 12% savings—net positive for ROIC 18.2%.  

Operator:  
Our next question comes from Emily Rodriguez with Bank of America.  

Emily Rodriguez:  
What are your expectations for pricing elasticity in the coming quarters?  

Sarah Chen:  
Hi Emily. Elasticity remains favorable at -2.1 overall, supporting 5-7% pricing across 70% portfolio with minimal 1.2% volume impact, like PepsiCo's Frito-Lay. Premium SKUs like NutriFuel low-sugar (15% snacks) and VitalQuench hold firm, NA +6.5%, EMEA +4% promo resets. Data-driven AI on Nielsen/IRI analyzes elasticity real-time, sustaining realization outpacing 2-3% inflation. Marketing amplifies: Refresh Everyday +22% HHP despite prices, Snack Smarter velocity +17%. Q4 seasonal strength, FY24 200 bps margin expansion assumes +1% volumes premium-skewed. Risks if inflation eases fast, but premiumization to 35% portfolio insulates.  

Operator:  
There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to Jamie Thompson for closing remarks.  

Jamie Thompson:  
Thank you, Operator, and thank you all for your insightful questions. These results validate our priorities delivering share gains, margin durability, and 8-10% EPS compounding. We're raising FY24 organic to 4.5-5.0%, EPS $5.65-5.75, margins 22.0-22.5%, with $500 million productivity and 20+ innovations for 6-8% organic. Risks like commodities persist, but $2.8 billion liquidity positions us for bolt-ons. We remain committed to strong results and shareholder value. Looking forward to next quarter.  

Alex Rivera:  
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the GCB Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
